transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, what brings me in is... I'm just really exhausted. It's a kind of tired that sleep doesn't seem to fix. Just getting through a normal workday, and then coming home and doing dinner—it all just feels a lot heavier than it should right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yes, I have. Most days lately, I just wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling. It's almost like I'm already disappointed in the day before it even starts. So, yes, I've definitely been feeling down.
Have you been finding it hard to enjoy things you usually like?

Yeah, I have. Normally, I really love painting, or... or just wandering through museum exhibits. It's usually a big part of my downtime. But recently, I just leave my art supplies sitting there untouched. I just can't seem to make myself care enough to actually go out and do any of it.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I feel really drained and unhappy, but I don't want to hurt myself. I don't feel like life isn't worth living, it's just... a bit of a struggle to get through the days right now. But no, no thoughts of harming myself.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about a month. Um, before this started, I was actually feeling unusually energized and... just really driven. But then it swung into this persistently low mood. So, yeah, this current feeling has been going on for about four weeks now.
During that unusually energized period before this low mood started, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I did. Um, during that stretch, I was sleeping maybe four hours a night. But I wasn't tired at all. I'd wake up feeling completely ready to go—like, ready to send out work emails, sketch out some event ideas, or even just reorganize the kitchen. I just didn't seem to need much rest at the time.
During that unusually energized period, did you feel unusually confident or important, more than is typical for you?

Yes, I think I did. Um, I was honestly convinced that I could fix the whole department morale problem at work. And, you know, our family routines at home, too. I just felt like... if everyone would just get on board with my plan, I could solve all of it. So, yeah, I definitely felt a lot more sure of myself and my ideas than I normally do.
During that unusually energized period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life, like at work, at home, or with other people?

No, it didn't cause any serious problems. If anything, I was just getting a lot done back then. 

It's actually more recently, with this low mood, that things have been a bit harder. I mean, I’m still showing up for work and handling my home responsibilities, so nothing is falling apart. But... I’ve definitely been slower with making decisions at the office. And I guess I've been less reliable with our family plans lately. I've also been a lot more withdrawn from the art activities that usually keep me connected. So, no major disasters, just... things are taking a lot more effort right now.
During that unusually energized period, were you talking more than usual?

Yeah, I was. Actually, my husband and a couple of my coworkers pointed it out to me at the time. They told me I was talking so fast, and just... jumping into conversations so much that they couldn’t really get a word in.
During that unusually energized period, were you more active or taking on more projects than you normally would?

Yes, I definitely was. Um, I signed myself up to lead extra pieces of that morale program at work. And I also volunteered for more Latino arts events... it was just far more than I would normally ever take on at one time.
About how many days did that unusually energized period last?
Um, I'm not really sure exactly. I didn't track it or count the days. It just... it lasted for a little while, but I couldn't give you a specific number.
Thinking back to that energized period, did it last at least four days in a row?
Um, I really couldn't say for sure. Like I mentioned, I wasn't keeping track of it at the time. It definitely went on for a little while, but I just don't know if it was four days in a row or not.
During that energized period, were you ever hospitalized because of it?
No, definitely not. Um, I was never in the hospital for it or anything like that. It didn't get out of hand in that way, I was just really busy.
During that energized period, were you taking on more projects or activities than you usually do?

Yes, I did, actually. I, um, I signed myself up to lead extra pieces of the morale program at work. And I also volunteered for a lot more Latino arts events. It was... well, it was far more than I would normally take on all at once.
During that unusually energized period, did you have any experiences where you were hearing or seeing things that other people couldn’t, or strongly believed something others said wasn’t true?

No, definitely not. Um, I never heard or saw anything that wasn't there. And I didn't have any strange beliefs or anything like that, either. I was just really energetic and busy, but nothing like what you're describing.
Thinking back to that unusually energized period, did it last at least 7 days in a row?
No, I don't think it was quite that long. Um, it was probably more like four or five days, maybe? But definitely not a full week in a row.
